summary: Yi-hsun Huang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner, and taught Huidi Zeng.

Yifa is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at National Taiwan University, the University of Hawaii, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. She held posts at the University of the West (~1996–2003) and Harvard University (2001–2002).

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~1994–1999). He held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem around 2011.

Yiliang Zhou was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University under Yinke Chen, and Harvard University, later serving as professor at Peking University (~1952–2001).

Yin Shun was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and at Minnan, Wuchang, and Taisho University. He taught at Minnan and Wuchang, served as president of the Hong Kong Buddhist Association (~1950–1952), and held later posts in Taiwan.

Ying-shih Yü was a scholar of Sinology, history, and philosophy who studied at Kansai University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Harvard University. He held professorships at the University of Michigan, Yale University (~1977–1987), and Princeton University (~1987–2021).
Yingguang Qu worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under traditional teachers Nordan Hutuktu in 1926 and Bai Puren in 1929.

Yinke Chen was a scholar of history, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Fudan, Berlin, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard. He held academic posts at Tsinghua University (~1925–1937), Peking University (~1946–1948), and Sun Yat-sen University (~1949–1969).
Yiu Wing Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong in 2013 under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yiu-ming Fung works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong in 1984 and served as Acting Head of the Division of Humanities at Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2008–2009).

Yohei Kawajiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013) and as a special researcher with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).
Yoichi Fukuda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and served as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003 and 2015).
Yong Hua Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).
Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche.
Yongshan He is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at McMaster University under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn, as well as teachers Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at Tsinghua University and Harvard University, and held a post in the Philosophy Department at Peking University in 1949.

Yonten Gyatso was a scholar of Tibetology and history who earned a Geshé degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and a diploma at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he later served as research advisor for Tibetan Studies.

Yoshifumi Honjo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Sakurabe. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, Kobe Women's University, Otani University, and Bukkyo University.

Yoshihide Yoshizu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a doctorate in Buddhist studies at Komazawa University, where he subsequently served as a lecturer (~1972–2014) and professor (~1985–2014).
Yoshihiko Nasu is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and held leadership posts at Kongojushinkai and Kongoju (attested 2017).
